Stated Claim / Post Context:
Australia's tax office announces it will ban credit card payments

The move is expected to affect taxpayers who currently use credit cards to pay their tax, including those with existing payment plans linked to a credit card.

Actual Article Body:
By DUNCAN MURRAY AND MAEVE BANNISTER IN SYDNEY FOR AUSTRALIAN ASSOCIATED PRESS

Published:  19:50 AEST, 1 October 2026   |  Updated:  20:43 AEST, 1 October 2026

Australians will no longer be able to pay their tax bills with a credit card after November 30, 2026, under a major change announced by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO).

The ATO said it would stop accepting credit cards following the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) review of merchant card payment costs and surcharging.

'As a government agency, the ATO has decided it would not be appropriate for the cost of credit card merchant fees to be transferred to the community,' the tax office said.

The move is expected to affect taxpayers who currently use credit cards to pay their tax, including those with existing payment plans linked to a credit card.
